units.leftText: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the overseers and servants:
units.rightText: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus,

units.leftText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: I thank my God whenever I remember you,
units.rightText: I thank my God every time I remember you.

units.leftText: always in every request of mine on behalf of you all, making my requests with joy,
units.rightText: In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy,

units.leftText: for your partnership in furtherance of the Good News from the first day until now;
units.rightText: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now,
leftNotes: 1:5 The word translated “partnership” (κοινωνίᾳ) also means “fellowship” and “sharing”.

units.leftText: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: being confident of this, that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: It is even right for me to think this way on behalf of all of you, because I have you in my heart, because both in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation of the Good News, you all are partakers with me of grace.
units.rightText: It is right for me to feel this way about all of you, since I have you in my heart. For in my chains and in my defense and confirmation of the gospel, you are all partners in grace with me.

units.leftText: For God is my witness, how I long after all of you in the tender mercies of Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: God is my witness how I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: This I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and all discernment,
units.rightText: And this is my prayer: that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and depth of insight,

units.leftText: so that you may approve the things that are excellent, that you may be sincere and without offense to the day of Christ,
units.rightText: so that you may be able to test and prove what is best and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ,

units.leftText: being filled with the fruits of righteousness which are through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
units.rightText: filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.

units.leftText: Now I desire to have you know, brothers, that the things which happened to me have turned out rather to the progress of the Good News,
units.rightText: Now I want you to know, brothers, that my circumstances have actually served to advance the gospel.
leftNotes: 1:12 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: so that it became evident to the whole palace guard, and to all the rest, that my bonds are in Christ,
units.rightText: As a result, it has become clear throughout the whole palace guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.

units.leftText: and that most of the brothers in the Lord, being confident through my bonds, are more abundantly bold to speak the word of God without fear.
units.rightText: And most of the brothers, confident in the Lord by my chains, now dare more greatly to speak the word without fear.
rightNotes: 1:14 NE and WH the word of God

units.leftText: Some indeed preach Christ even out of envy and strife, and some also out of good will.
units.rightText: It is true that some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others out of goodwill.

units.leftText: The former insincerely preach Christ from selfish ambition, thinking that they add affliction to my chains;
units.rightText: The latter do so in love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel.
rightNotes: 1:16 BYZ and TR reverse the order of verses 16 and 17.

units.leftText: but the latter out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the Good News.
units.rightText: The former, however, preach Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, supposing that they can add to the distress of my chains.

units.leftText: What does it matter? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed. I rejoice in this, yes, and will rejoice.
units.rightText: What then is the issue? Just this: that in every way, whether by false motives or true, Christ is preached. And in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will continue to rejoice,

units.leftText: For I know that this will turn out to my salvation through your prayers and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: because I know that through your prayers and the provision of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, my distress will turn out for my deliverance.

units.leftText: according to my earnest expectation and hope, that I will in no way be disappointed, but with all boldness, as always, now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.
units.rightText: I eagerly expect and hope that I will in no way be ashamed, but will have complete boldness so that now as always Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death.

units.leftText: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
units.rightText: For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

units.leftText: But if I live on in the flesh, this will bring fruit from my work; yet I don’t know what I will choose.
units.rightText: But if I go on living in the body, this will mean fruitful labor for me. So what shall I choose? I do not know.

units.leftText: But I am hard pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better.
units.rightText: I am torn between the two. I desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better indeed.

units.leftText: Yet to remain in the flesh is more needful for your sake.
units.rightText: But it is more necessary for you that I remain in the body.

units.leftText: Having this confidence, I know that I will remain, yes, and remain with you all for your progress and joy in the faith,
units.rightText: Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and will continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith,

units.leftText: that your boasting may abound in Christ Jesus in me through my presence with you again.
units.rightText: so that through my coming to you again your exultation in Christ Jesus will resound on account of me.

units.leftText: Only let your way of life be worthy of the Good News of Christ, that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear of your state, that you stand firm in one spirit, with one soul striving for the faith of the Good News;
units.rightText: Nevertheless, conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you in my absence, I will know that you stand firm in one spirit, contending together as one for the faith of the gospel,
rightNotes: 1:27 Or striving together with one mind

units.leftText: and in nothing frightened by the adversaries, which is for them a proof of destruction, but to you of salvation, and that from God.
units.rightText: without being frightened in any way by those who oppose you. This is a clear sign of their destruction but of your salvation, and it is from God.

units.leftText: Because it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer on his behalf,
units.rightText: For it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for Him,

units.leftText: having the same conflict which you saw in me and now hear is in me.
units.rightText: since you are encountering the same struggle you saw I had, and now hear that I still have.

units.leftText: If therefore there is any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
units.rightText: Therefore if you have any encouragement in Christ, if any comfort from His love, if any fellowship with the Spirit, if any affection and compassion,

units.leftText: make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
units.rightText: then make my joy complete by being like-minded, having the same love, being united in spirit and purpose.

units.leftText: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
units.rightText: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty pride, but in humility consider others more important than yourselves.

units.leftText: each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
units.rightText: Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.

units.leftText: Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus:

units.leftText: who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
units.rightText: Who, existing in the form of God,

units.leftText: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.
units.rightText: but emptied Himself,

units.leftText: And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.
units.rightText: And being found in appearance as a man,

units.leftText: Therefore God also highly exalted him, and gave to him the name which is above every name,
units.rightText: Therefore God exalted Him to the highest place

units.leftText: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth,
units.rightText: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow,

units.leftText: and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
units.rightText: and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord,

units.leftText: So then, my beloved, even as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
units.rightText: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.

units.leftText: For it is God who works in you both to will and to work for his good pleasure.
units.rightText: For it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose.

units.leftText: Do all things without complaining and arguing,
units.rightText: Do everything without complaining or arguing,

units.leftText: that you may become blameless and harmless, children of God without defect in the middle of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you are seen as lights in the world,
units.rightText: so that you may be blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation, in which you shine as lights in the world

units.leftText: holding up the word of life, that I may have something to boast in the day of Christ that I didn’t run in vain nor labor in vain.
units.rightText: as you hold forth the word of life, in order that I may boast on the day of Christ that I did not run or labor in vain.

units.leftText: Yes, and if I am poured out on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice with you all.
units.rightText: But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice with all of you.

units.leftText: In the same way, you also should be glad and rejoice with me.
units.rightText: So you too should be glad and rejoice with me.

units.leftText: But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, that I also may be cheered up when I know how you are doing.
units.rightText: Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, that I also may be cheered when I learn how you are doing.

units.leftText: For I have no one else like-minded, who will truly care about you.
units.rightText: I have nobody else like him who will genuinely care for your needs.

units.leftText: For they all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For all the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: But you know that he has proved himself. As a child serves a father, so he served with me in furtherance of the Good News.
units.rightText: But you know Timothy’s proven worth, that as a child with his father he has served with me to advance the gospel.

units.leftText: Therefore I hope to send him at once, as soon as I see how it will go with me.
units.rightText: So I hope to send him as soon as I see what happens with me.

units.leftText: But I trust in the Lord that I myself also will come shortly.
units.rightText: And I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon.

units.leftText: But I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, fellow soldier, and your apostle and servant of my need,
units.rightText: But I thought it necessary to send back to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, who is also your messenger and minister to my needs.

units.leftText: since he longed for you all, and was very troubled because you had heard that he was sick.
units.rightText: For he has been longing for all of you and is distressed because you heard he was ill.

units.leftText: For indeed he was sick nearly to death, but God had mercy on him, and not on him only, but on me also, that I might not have sorrow on sorrow.
units.rightText: He was sick indeed, nearly unto death. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, to spare me sorrow upon sorrow.

units.leftText: I have sent him therefore the more diligently, that when you see him again, you may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.
units.rightText: Therefore I am all the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less anxious.

units.leftText: Receive him therefore in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
units.rightText: Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor men like him,

units.leftText: because for the work of Christ he came near to death, risking his life to supply that which was lacking in your service toward me.
units.rightText: because he nearly died for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up for your deficit of service to me.

units.leftText: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord! To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not tiresome, but for you it is safe.
units.rightText: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again, and it is a safeguard for you.

units.leftText: Beware of the dogs; beware of the evil workers; beware of the false circumcision.
units.rightText: Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!

units.leftText: For we are the circumcision, who worship God in the Spirit, and rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh;
units.rightText: For it is we who are the circumcision, we who worship by the Spirit of God, who glory in Christ Jesus, and who put no confidence in the flesh —

units.leftText: though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh. If any other man thinks that he has confidence in the flesh, I yet more:
units.rightText: though I myself could have such confidence.

units.leftText: circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; concerning the law, a Pharisee;
units.rightText: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin; a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;

units.leftText: concerning zeal, persecuting the assembly; concerning the righteousness which is in the law, found blameless.
units.rightText: as to zeal, persecuting the church; as to righteousness in the law, faultless.

units.leftText: However, I consider those things that were gain to me as a loss for Christ.
units.rightText: But whatever was gain to me I count as loss for the sake of Christ.

units.leftText: Yes most certainly, and I count all things to be a loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, my Lord, for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and count them nothing but refuse, that I may gain Christ
units.rightText: More than that, I count all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have lost all things. I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ

units.leftText: and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own, that which is of the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith,
units.rightText: and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God on the basis of faith.
rightNotes: 3:9 Or through the faithfulness of Christ

units.leftText: that I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed to his death,
units.rightText: I want to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death,

units.leftText: if by any means I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.
units.rightText: and so, somehow, to attain to the resurrection from the dead.

units.leftText: Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect; but I press on, that I may take hold of that for which also I was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: Not that I have already obtained all this, or have already been made perfect, but I press on to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of me.

units.leftText: Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do: forgetting the things which are behind and stretching forward to the things which are before,
units.rightText: Brothers, I do not consider myself yet to have taken hold of it. But one thing I do: Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead,

units.leftText: I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God’s heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, think this way. If in anything you think otherwise, God will also reveal that to you.
units.rightText: All of us who are mature should embrace this point of view. And if you think differently about some issue, God will reveal this to you as well.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, to the extent that we have already attained, let’s walk by the same rule. Let’s be of the same mind.
units.rightText: Nevertheless, we must live up to what we have already attained.

units.leftText: Brothers, be imitators together of me, and note those who walk this way, even as you have us for an example.
units.rightText: Join one another in following my example, brothers, and carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern we set for you.

units.leftText: For many walk, of whom I told you often, and now tell you even weeping, as the enemies of the cross of Christ,
units.rightText: For as I have often told you before, and now say again even with tears: Many live as enemies of the cross of Christ.

units.leftText: whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who think about earthly things.
units.rightText: Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame. Their minds are set on earthly things.

units.leftText: For our citizenship is in heaven, from where we also wait for a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ,

units.leftText: who will change the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working by which he is able even to subject all things to himself.
units.rightText: who, by the power that enables Him to subject all things to Himself, will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.

units.leftText: Therefore, my brothers, beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, my beloved.
units.rightText: Therefore, my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, that is how you must stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.

units.leftText: I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to think the same way in the Lord.
units.rightText: I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.

units.leftText: Yes, I beg you also, true partner, help these women, for they labored with me in the Good News with Clement also, and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.
units.rightText: Yes, and I ask you, my true yokefellow, to help these women who have contended at my side for the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the Book of Life.
rightNotes: 4:3 Or I ask you, loyal Syzygus

units.leftText: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!”
units.rightText: Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!

units.leftText: Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand.
units.rightText: Let your gentleness be apparent to all. The Lord is near.

units.leftText: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
units.rightText: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

units.leftText: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report: if there is any virtue and if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
units.rightText: Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable — if anything is excellent or praiseworthy — think on these things.

units.leftText: Do the things which you learned, received, heard, and saw in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
units.rightText: Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me, put it into practice. And the God of peace will be with you.

units.leftText: But I rejoice in the Lord greatly that now at length you have revived your thought for me; in which you did indeed take thought, but you lacked opportunity.
units.rightText: Now I rejoice greatly in the Lord that at last you have revived your concern for me. You were indeed concerned, but you had no opportunity to show it.

units.leftText: Not that I speak because of lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.
units.rightText: I am not saying this out of need, for I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances.

units.leftText: I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. In any and all circumstances I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need.
units.rightText: I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound. In any and every situation I have learned the secret of being filled and being hungry, of having plenty and having need.

units.leftText: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
units.rightText: I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.
rightNotes: 4:13 NA, SBL, NE, and WH in the One who gives me strength. BYZ and TR in Christ who gives me strength.

units.leftText: However you did well that you shared in my affliction.
units.rightText: Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my affliction.

units.leftText: You yourselves also know, you Philippians, that in the beginning of the Good News, when I departed from Macedonia, no assembly shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving but you only.
units.rightText: And as you Philippians know, in the early days of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church but you partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving.

units.leftText: For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to my need.
units.rightText: For even while I was in Thessalonica, you provided for my needs again and again.

units.leftText: Not that I seek for the gift, but I seek for the fruit that increases to your account.
units.rightText: Not that I am seeking a gift, but I am looking for the fruit that may be credited to your account.

units.leftText: But I have all things and abound. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things that came from you, a sweet-smelling fragrance, an acceptable and well-pleasing sacrifice to God.
units.rightText: I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus. They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.

units.leftText: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Now to our God and Father be the glory forever and ever! Amen.
units.rightText: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.

units.leftText: Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.
units.rightText: Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: All the saints greet you, especially those who are of Caesar’s household.
units.rightText: All the saints send you greetings, especially those from the household of Caesar.

units.leftText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
units.rightText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
